source.title: Reinforcement Learning for Optimized Trade Execution

claims.statement: The private state includes elapsed time and remaining inventory; public market variables are separate.

claims.locator: Section 3, PDF pages 3–4, cost update and pseudocode
claims.statement: Training moves backward through the finite horizon and averages immediate payoff plus optimal next-state value for each state-action.
claims.implementation: ExecutionValueLearning.train: ascending remaining-time lattice and incremental observed mean

claims.statement: When the horizon expires, remaining inventory must be executed.
claims.implementation: ExecutionValueLearning._actions: time-one action equals all remaining units

chosen_variant: Four decision intervals, four-unit buy program and empirical finite-horizon value table
adaptations: The paper's action is a limit-price revision for all remaining shares, with queue priority, partial fills and mandatory terminal market execution. Here an action is the number of whole units to buy with a next-tick market target; no standing limit orders or queue model are claimed.

The training lattice uses synthetic rewards and three pressure states. It covers all private states and actions but does not use NASDAQ INET order-flow records, original cost normalization or market-impact simulation.
Each five-tick demonstration episode resets the target position for the next buy program. The reset is an adapter device, not part of the paper's execution objective.
